name: Black Death across France
summary: The plague reaches Marseille in autumn 1347 and Avignon by January 1348, killing perhaps half the city's population. Pope Clement VI remains in his palace; his physician Guy de Chauliac documents the two clinical forms (bubonic, pneumonic). By summer 1349 the disease has covered France.

_quarry.structural_significance: Loss of one-third to half the French population disrupts the Hundred Years' War for a decade; the 1351 Ordonnance attempts to fix wages and prices in vain; large-scale labour shortages permanently shift rural tenure terms in favour of peasants.
